Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), as in the old capture_bps set: Credo ships cables, chips and modules to ODMs and module makers a quarter or two before the racks are capitalised. Growth: LightCounting's latest forecast, +120% for 2026 and +76% for 2027, declining to +20% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-10-08 [src 32]); the January vintage was +60% for 2026 [src 31].
drivers.derivation: CY2026 16.5 x 2.20 = $36.3B; CY2027 36.3 x 1.76 = $63.888B; CY2028: LightCounting's optics-to-capex ratio (Kilian 2026-10-27 17:21Z, replacing the straight-line interpolation of growth rates): optics sales to the top five cloud providers were 2.7% of their capex in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026, rising to 4.1% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on LightCounting's 'Optics for AI Clusters' [src 33]); linear between 2026 and 2031 (+0.2pt a year) gives 3.3% in 2027 and 3.5% in 2028. CY2028 growth = (Big-4 capex 1,330 / 1,080) x (3.5% / 3.3%) = 1.2315 x 1.0606 = 1.306; 63.888 x 1.306 = $83.438B. Cross-check: the pluggable transceiver market grows from 60 million units in 2026 to 175 million by 2030 (CEO quoting market forecasters, Q1 FY27 call [src 22]), (175/60)^(1/4) - 1 = +30.7% a year in units. CY2026-27 keep LightCounting's published growth rates (+120%, +76%) because they are published figures; the same ratio method would give +57% for 2027 (1,080/733 x 3.3/3.1), so the 2027 step is the richer of the two. Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), as in the old capture_bps set: Credo ships cables, chips and modules to ODMs and module makers a quarter or two before the racks are capitalised. Variants: CY2028 tied to Big-4 capex growth alone (+23%, $78.7B) gives research target (12m) 220.69 (-1.0%); the earlier straight-line interpolation of LightCounting growth rates (+62%, $103.5B) gives 232.78 (+4.4%). LightCounting's 2026 growth forecast was raised from +60% (January [src 31]) to +120% (October [src 32]). Vintage gap: our CY2026 $36.3B (16.5 x 2.20, October vintage) is above the $26B for 2026 in LightCounting's January vintage as quoted by POET [src 31] (36.3 / 26 - 1 = +40%); the October +120% is the newer figure, so it is used. drivers.source: FY2026 10-K end-customer table: Customer D 33%, Customer B 32%, Customer E 19% (direct-billing basis Customer A 49%) [src 12]. Q1 FY27 10-Q end-customer table: D 33%, C 28%, E 13%, F 10% (direct basis A 43%, 57% of receivables) [src 11]; CFO: 'our largest customer was a third of our revenue at 33%' [src 22].
drivers.derivation: Base 0.33 (FY26) and held at 0.33 in FY27-29 (Q1 FY27 33%; management expects 3-4 customers above 10% [src 22], i.e. diversification comes through the other customers, which the shares carry). Formula: each segment's revenue = TAM x share x 1000 x (1 - 0.33) / (1 - top_customer_pct). At the base path the factor is 1. Moving the driver to T means the top customer buys less (or more) while every other customer stays as the TAM x share build says: total revenue scales by 0.67 / (1 - T) and the top customer's revenue by T x 0.67 / (0.33 x (1 - T)). Bear: T 0.33 -> 0.21 cuts total revenue 15.2% and the top customer's revenue 46% (a 1.6T AEC dual-source to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices, agents 1-5). The top customer's product mix is not disclosed; the term applies to copper and optical alike (the CFO says these hyperscalers buy more than AECs [src 22]). Variant view: on the direct-billing basis (43%) the same customer-loss story is larger; the end-customer basis is used because the sourcing decision is the end customer's. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): 0.33 every quarter: FY26 10-K end-customer D 33% (the FY figure is used for each FY26 quarter: an annual concentration figure applied to each base quarter, so the base quarters aggregate to the 10-K's 0.33; the 10-Q end-customer tables give the quarter's largest end customer at 35% Q1 (acc 0001807794-25-000021), 42% Q2 (0001628280-25-054549), 39% Q3 (0001628280-26-014017), Q4 not disclosed, with the letters rotating between filings, so the quarter tops are not the FY top); Q1 FY27 10-Q D 33% [src 11]; held forward.
